jobs.description: Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d)The Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) of the Max Planck Society, located on the research campus in Garching near Munich, is a leading facility for the development of highly precise radiation sensors and detector systems. On approximately 1,400 m² of cleanroom space, HLL develops, fabricates and tests advanced semiconductor detectors for applications in X-ray astronomy, particle physics and materials research. With around 50 employees from different nationalities, HLL provides a highly international and interdisciplinary environment in which scientists, engineers and technology specialists work closely together across the entire development chain — from fundamental research and simulation to device design, fabrication and experimental characterization.To strengthen our activities in quantum sensing and advanced quantum-device technologies, and to provide scientific and technological support to our research, engineering and service teams, we are looking for a Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) to join our team at the earliest possible date on a full-time basis (39 hours/week). Your responsibilities- Develop and optimize quantum sensor concepts based on qubit systems and quantum effects.- Perform advanced numerical simulations and modeling of qubit-based sensing systems, including relevant physical processes, noise sources and system-level performance.- Work closely with technology development, engineering and experimental teams to translate simulation results into practical implementations.- Analyze experimental data and use the results to refine physical models and sensor designs.- Contribute to scientific publications, technical documentation and intellectual property.Your profile- PhD in physics, electrical engineering, applied physics, quantum engineering or a related field.- Background in quantum sensing, qubit control and precision measurement.- Experience with numerical simulation, modeling and system design.- Analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a practical, technology-oriented mindset.- Strong motivation to work in close cooperation with technology, engineering and experimental teams.- Fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage.Advantageous experienceExperience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:- Cleanroom / semiconductor / microfabrication experience- Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, COMSOL or equivalent - MEMS/NEMS or integrated sensor technologies- Precision measurement and low-noise instrumentation- Experience bridging qubit physics, device design and fabrication technologyWhat we offer- International environment, diverse responsibilities and a high degree of autonomy: Flat hierarchies and a collaborative, agile team within an internationally renowned research institution. You will work closely with scientists, engineers and technology specialists across disciplines and have the opportunity to shape the development of innovative quantum-sensing technologies.- Advantages of the public sector: Remuneration according to the German public service pay scale TVöD (Bund), depending on qualifications and experience; occupational pension scheme (VBL); 30 days of annual leave (31 days as of 2027), plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. The position is initially limited to two years, with the possibility of subsequent permanent employment.- Work-life balance and compatibility of family and career: Flexible working hours (flextime), opportunities for mobile working, support in finding childcare and care for family members, and a comprehensive company health management program.- Professional development: Thorough onboarding and opportunities for internal and external training and further education tailored to your individual needs. You will have the opportunity to continuously develop your expertise in quantum sensing, qubit technology, simulation and semiconductor technology.- Research campus: Excellent access by public transport, including the possibility of a monthly subsidy for the “Deutschland-Job-Ticket”, or by car with free parking in the immediate vicinity of the laboratory. A canteen and further dining options are available nearby, as well as campus-wide events and activities.The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply.Further information and applicationDetailed information about the Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) can be found at HLL – Semiconductor Laboratory (http://www.hll.mpg.de/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Jelena Ninkovic, Tel.: +49 89 839400-49.Please submit your application, including meaningful application documents, exclusively online via our application portal (https://bewerbermanagement.net/en/jobposting/6c80f90f47c14e1b28b7c86e27f035140c44c8f20/apply) by 31 October 2026. Include the names of three referees that can be contacted in your CV.We look forward to receiving your application! That's why we invite you to take on new challenges, test your ideas, and celebrate success. jobs.description: Structural Engineer (all genders) - Material Testing & Structural ValidationHelp Accelerate Industrial DecarbonizationJoin exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.As our Structural Engineer – Material Testing & Structural Validation, you'll play a key role in developing the lightweight structural systems that make GlassPoint's technology reliable, safe, and scalable.Working closely with Structural, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Operations teams, you'll combine advanced engineering analysis with hands-on testing to validate innovative designs and ensure they perform under real-world conditions. From small-scale material characterization to full-scale component testing, your work will directly influence the next generation of technology. Your ImpactThe structures you validate will become part of some of the world's largest industrial solar thermal plants, helping heavy industry reduce emissions while improving energy security.You'll combine engineering theory with practical experimentation, transforming test results into optimized designs and helping GlassPoint continuously improve the performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of its technology.What You'll DoDesign & Improve Structural Systems- Analyze and optimize lightweight structural systems, components, and structural connections.- Evaluate the behavior of steel, aluminum, composite materials, and ETFE film systems.- Support the development of innovative structural concepts for industrial solar thermal applications.- Transform engineering insights into scalable, manufacturable design improvements.Lead Material & Component Testing- Plan, build, execute, and evaluate material and component tests.- Design and instrument full-scale structural testing.- Conduct small-specimen material testing to characterize material behavior.- Analyze test results and translate findings into engineering recommendations.Develop & Validate Engineering Models- Develop, calibrate, and improve nonlinear finite element (FEA) models.- Predict structural behavior using numerical simulations.- Validate simulation results through physical testing.- Continuously refine engineering models to improve design accuracy.Collaborate Across Engineering- Work closely with Structural, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Operations teams.- Support design decisions through data-driven engineering.- Contribute to solving complex structural challenges across international projects.- Share technical expertise and help drive continuous innovation.Who You AreYou're someone who enjoys solving complex engineering challenges and turning analysis into practical solutions.You combine analytical thinking with a hands-on mindset and enjoy moving between simulations, laboratory testing, and real-world engineering. You're curious, collaborative, and motivated by seeing your work become part of technologies that make a global impact.Ideally, you'll bring:- A degree in Structural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline (ideally with a background in construction, civil engineering, or automotive engineering).- Several years of experience in structural, material, or component testing.- Experience working with nonlinear material behavior and structural analysis.- Strong experience with numerical modelling and nonlinear FEA.- Hands-on experience planning and executing engineering tests.- Familiarity with sensors, instrumentation, and measurement systems.- A structured, analytical, and independent working style.- Confidence working in an international engineering environment.- Excellent English communication skills; German is an advantage.- Experience with foundation systems for solar structures, soil testing, rammed piles, ground screws, or percussion drilling is a plus.What You'll Find at GlassPoint- Real ownership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact from day one.- Exceptional colleagues from diverse disciplines who challenge, support, and learn from each other.- Complex challenges that require curiosity, collaboration, and innovation.- An international team united by a shared purpose and ambitious goals.- The adventure of helping build the future of industrial decarbonization. We value inclusion and foster a culture of belonging, welcoming team members of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, gender identity, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We have zero tolerance for discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation. GlassPoint helps heavy industry decarbonize by replacing fuel-based steam with solar thermal heat. This reduces energy costs and improves long-term energy security.
